headline: Indigenous Women Help 208 Baby Turtles Reach the Amazon
meta_description: Seven Indigenous women in Ecuador's Amazon protected turtle eggs from flooding, predators and pollution, successfully releasing 208 hatchlings to the wild.
summary_short: Seven Indigenous women in Ecuador's Amazon have successfully guided 208 baby turtles into the wild after protecting their eggs from threats.
body:
Seven Indigenous women in Ecuador's Amazon have successfully protected and hatched 208 baby turtles, guiding them safely back to the wild. Known as the "turtle women," these guardians collected 235 eggs and shielded them through a vulnerable period when flooding, predators, and pollution pose constant threats to survival.

The work reflects both deep ecological knowledge and urgent conservation need. By intervening during the eggs' most fragile stage—before hatchlings could fend for themselves—the women increased the chances that these turtles would reach adulthood and contribute to healthy populations in the Amazon ecosystem.

Their efforts underscore how Indigenous communities remain essential stewards of biodiversity. In a region where external pressures mount daily, these women's patient work demonstrates that local action, rooted in place-based understanding, can turn the tide for vulnerable species.
quick_facts: Seven Indigenous women in Ecuador's Amazon
208 baby turtles successfully released to the wild
235 eggs collected and protected from flooding, predators, pollution
